answer: Hardware clock-skew fingerprinting can anchor identity. Every oscillator drifts at a device-specific rate, so an auditor compares timestamp jitter across two hundred signed messages; aliases minted on one box share a skew signature within fifty microseconds, so a garden of apparent independence collapses into one payout. A farm buying a thousand machines pays real capital, its fable of independence collapsing into identical clocks. Sampling is passive, using timestamps the ledger holds, so honest agents pay nothing, each drift record on a basalt foundation nobody rewrites.
